name: Olive-Buff
lede: Olive-Buff is a descriptive pairing of olive and buff, carried forward from Ridgway's 1886 Nomenclature of Colors.

sections.title: Two pale nature words, paired
sections.body:
The library carries this name forward from Ridgway's 1886 *Nomenclature of Colors*, and it is also plotted on Ridgway's 1912 plate XL, hue 21 triple-prime, tone d [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 lists classify it as a pale yellow, lighter and flatter than either word alone would suggest [1]. [[olive]] usually reads as a muted green and [[buff]] as a warm tan; paired and paled together, the result sits closer to a dusty beige than to either source word [1].

The nearest named color in the library is Pale Olive-Buff, about 4.2 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[natural|Natural]] and [[lion|Lion]] not far behind [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 79, chroma 18, hue 92 degrees, Munsell 3.5Y 7.8/2.5 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 3,241 of 23,781 paintings, 13.63 percent, as photographed [2]. That makes it one of the more common named colors we track, not a rarity [2]. It peaks in the 1790s, in 102 of that decade's 385 paintings, about 1.9 times the expected rate [2]. Willem van de Velde the Elder is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 12 of his 14 works, over 6 times the baseline [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].

origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature (1912); ColorHub library
